simple.meaning: מִמְכָּר (mimkâr) is a Hebrew action word meaning “merchandise ; abstractly, a selling.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 10 times in Leviticus, Deuteronomy, Nehemiah, Ezekiel, beginning at Leviticus 25:14. The surrounding contexts include family, city, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to מִמְכָּר (H4465) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: מִמְכָּר (mimkâr) / H4465 is traced through Leviticus 25:14, Leviticus 25:25, Leviticus 25:27, Leviticus 25:28 with source-language evidence and verse context.

On Deut 18:8 see מֶכֶר .

occurrences.englishText: “ ‘If you sell anything to your neighbor, or buy from your neighbor, you shall not wrong one another.
“ ‘If your brother becomes poor, and sells some of his possessions, then his kinsman who is next to him shall come, and redeem that which his brother has sold.
then let him reckon the years since its sale, and restore the surplus to the man to whom he sold it; and he shall return to his property.

But if he isn’t able to get it back for himself, then what he has sold shall remain in the hand of him who has bought it until the Year of Jubilee. In the Jubilee it shall be released, and he shall return to his property.
“ ‘If a man sells a dwelling house in a walled city, then he may redeem it within a whole year after it has been sold. For a full year he shall have the right of redemption.

The Levites may redeem the house that was sold, and the city of his possession, and it shall be released in the Jubilee; for the houses of the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.

He shall reckon with him who bought him from the year that he sold himself to him to the Year of Jubilee. The price of his sale shall be according to the number of years; he shall be with him according to the time of a hired servant.
They shall have like portions to eat, in addition to that which comes from the sale of his family possessions.
So the merchants and sellers of all kinds of wares camped outside of Jerusalem once or twice.

For the seller won’t return to that which is sold, although they are still alive; for the vision concerns the whole multitude of it. None will return. None will strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.
